blocks.value: `++` and `--` will become second nature in Lesson 7, where nearly every loop ends with one.

`++` can go after the variable (`a++`) or before it (`++a`). On its own they are the same. Inside a larger statement, **postfix** `a++` uses the old value and then adds one, while **prefix** `++a` adds one first and then uses the new value:

int a = 5;
int b = a++;                   // b gets 5, then a becomes 6
System.out.println(a + " " + b);   // 6 5

int c = ++a;                   // a becomes 7, then c gets 7
System.out.println(a + " " + c);   // 7 7
